requirements.requirement: New login sessions on node1 default to C.UTF-8.
requirements.summary: The locale was changed from en_US.UTF-8 to C.UTF-8, and clean login shells directly reported LANG=C.UTF-8 with UTF-8 charmap both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: New services on node1 default to C.UTF-8.
requirements.summary: Fresh transient services directly reported LANG=C.UTF-8 and UTF-8 charmap before and after reboot. The persistent locale file and systemd manager environment also reported C.UTF-8 after reboot.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Node1 persistently defaults to C.UTF-8 for both new login sessions and new services. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, the reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and system health plus locale behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Setting the locale was the required change (cmd-59b16b6187ad4fea). The transient service runs were bounded behavior probes (cmd-ae1981a7850147e0, cmd-bee5f555587a46e9, cmd-436471de30d049bd), and the reboot scheduled by cmd-f7a2cdb13bbc450a fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. The first service-probe attempt failed, but subsequent inspection found no unit or journal, so it is not shown to have changed state (cmd-4dba012b04e54c3b, cmd-b8ed3d6f6b5a4599). Final snapshots show no failed services, new exposure, or damaged package state; temporary-file and PID changes are normal consequences of the required reboot.
